story_of_day.headline: Trump says US aid to Israel ends this year
story_of_day.story: On election morning Trump told Fox News the US will stop its roughly $4bn a year in military aid to Israel at the end of 2026, saying Israel does not need it. It is a verbal claim so far, with no policy detail. It lands as Netanyahu's bloc won the most seats in Israel's election but is about eight short of a majority, leaving Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties as kingmakers.
story_of_day.so_what: If real, it is a major shift in the US-Israel relationship, and also a pitch to voters tired of the Gaza war. Congress controls the money, so what the new House looks like matters. Treat it as a signal until a formal move follows.

last_time.text: Last run the focus was US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island alongside peace talks. Since then the talks were dismissed by Tehran, Iran warned against new attacks, and Yemen accused the IRGC and Hezbollah of sending 21 experts to back the Houthis.

cards.headline: Brent whipsaws $6 on peace-talk headlines
cards.story: Brent fell from $107 to $100.80 on Tuesday on reports of US-Iran progress, then bounced to about $104 after Tehran dismissed them. It had already dropped 7.6% on Monday. Separately, a report says Houthi fighters have made ground raids into Saudi Arabia.
cards.so_what: Oil is trading headlines, not barrels. Rystad does not expect Hormuz flows to be back to pre-war levels, even with a limited deal by mid-2027, so fuel prices stay high for a long time.

last_time.text: Brent was about $106 last run. It is now $104.42.

cards.headline: Ukraine strikes kill at least 38 in a day
cards.story: Russian attacks on an aid centre, a hospice and a hospital killed at least 38 people in 24 hours, and Zelensky warns more are under rubble. He still hopes Abu Dhabi talks can open a path to a meeting with Putin, while Germany's chancellor says Russia has not engaged seriously.
cards.so_what: Diplomacy and bombing are running side by side with no sign of a deal. Zelensky is openly linking the war to today's US vote.

last_time.text: Last run: the death toll at the aid centre was 29 with 48 missing. It has now risen.

cards.headline: Garment strikes shut nearly 1,000 factories
cards.story: Reports say almost 1,000 factories in the $40bn garment sector are closed as wage protests spread, with 16 more arrests in Mirpur. The government accuses ousted PM Hasina of fuelling the unrest, which the protesters deny. India says it is monitoring.
cards.so_what: Buyers watch reliability as much as price. A long shutdown risks orders moving to Vietnam or Cambodia, and the political blame game makes a quick wage deal harder.

last_time.text: Last run the protests had run several days with some factories reopening. The shutdown now looks wider and the arrests are rising.

cards.headline: Record turnout as polls open across the US
cards.story: Voting is under way, with record turnout reported in Florida, Georgia, Michigan and North Carolina. Texas has the most expensive Senate race in US history. The DoJ also told Democrats they could be targets of an Alaska ballot investigation.
cards.so_what: Results begin coming in during Sydney's morning. Control of the House decides how much Trump can be checked at home, including on spending like Israel aid.

last_time.text: Last run was election-day set-up. Voting is now actually happening.

watch.title: US midterm results
watch.text: Watch the House and Senate calls over the next 24 hours, then whether Trump's Israel aid line becomes formal policy or an election-day remark.

takes_review.text: Brent was $105.92 when I said don't chase oil. It is $104.42 now, after a $6 intraday swing, still inside my $98-115 range. The take is holding: big moves on headlines, no clear winner yet.
